newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Pacific to go ahead with Philippine spinoff.
newsitem.headline: First Pacific to go ahead with Philippine spinoff.

text.p: Blue chip First Pacific Co Ltd plans to spin off its Philippine arm Smart Communications in July despite a recent slump in the Philippine stock market, a top company official said on Monday.

"The spinoff of Smart Communications could be as early as July this year to September...depending on the scheduling," managing director Manuel Pangilinan said at a news conference. Investors have turned the heat on First Pacific since the Philippine stock market suffered a slump in the last week, set off by fears of a meltdown in the property sector.

First Pacific has considerable business exposure in the Philippines. Its Philippines flagship Metro Pacific Corp owns Smart Communications, the company's major mobile phone operations in the Philippines.
First Pacific's other Philippine unit Fort Bonifacio is involved in developing the former Fort Bonifacio military facility in Metro Manila into an upmarket metropolis.
While First Pacific was concerned with the slide in the stock market, Pangilinan told reporters he was confident its Philippine arms could weather problems ahead.
"Frankly, the state of the Philippine stock market does give us some concern," Pangilinan said.

"But even in the face of such conditions, it's our hope that concerns over the property market and banking sector in the Philippines would eventually be overcome by the time Smart Communications is listed," he said.
Pangilinan however played down fears of a property glut now gripping the Philippines, saying the oversupply would probably only be felt in 1999.
"Our feeling is that property fears are exaggerated. Unlike Thailand, the property glut does not exist, at least not yet in the Philippines," he said.
"The glut is not likely to happen physically, until some time in 1999," he said.
If and when the glut hit, Fort Bonifacio should also be able to hold its own, Pangilinan said.
"The market will split in a two-tier market. Those developers who focus on quality development projects and those who don't. I like to think that Fort Bonifacio is the former (category)."
